dossier.purpose: Glean is an open-source system (originated at Meta) for collecting, storing and querying typed facts about source code: symbol definitions, cross-references, hierarchies. Per-language indexers write facts into on-disk databases (RocksDB by default, experimental LMDB). The facts are queried with the Angle language through a CLI/shell, a Thrift server (HTTP transport by default per the cabal flag), a Haskell client library, the 'Glass' language-agnostic symbol server, and a generic read-only LSP server (glean-lsp) offering definition, references, hover, outline and symbol search. It indexes in batch and serves a static snapshot; the tree contains no MCP server, no Claude Code/Codex integration, and no editing or diagnostics features (evidence in the fields below).

claims.claim: Glean is a system for working with facts about source code: per-symbol information (location, type, relationships), cross-references such as function/method calls, and call hierarchies, type hierarchies, etc.

It is used for collecting and storing detailed information about code structure at scale, and for querying it (Angle query language) to power tools 'from online IDE features to offline code analysis'.
'There is currently full support for' C++ and C, Hack, Haskell, JavaScript/Flow and Python.
Also supports the SCIP or LSIF indexing formats, for Rust (via rust-analyzer), Go, TypeScript, Java, Python and Dotnet.
Custom indexers for Python, Java, Kotlin, Erlang, Thrift, Buck and Bazel, C# and Swift exist but 'aren't in the open source release yet'.
Glean is licensed under a BSD LICENSE.

Contributions via GitHub pull requests require signing the Contributor License Agreement; Haskell style is checked with hlint (80 columns, -Wall clean); C++ must compile with Clang or GCC; feedback via GitHub issues and a Discord server.
Building is documented in the 'Building Glean' page; that page states Linux only ('only tested on Linux so far'), built on x86_64 and arm64v8, using GHC and Cabal.

Docker demo: `docker run -ti -p8888:8888 ghcr.io/facebookincubator/glean/demo` (React codebase with hyperlinks); a variant mounts your own code (needs a .flowconfig) at /glean_demo/code; a `shell` argument drops into a shell with the glean binaries.

glean-lsp is 'a generic LSP server that provides a minimal set of LSP features using Glean data', works 'for any language supported by Glean and Glass', and provides Go to Definition, Go to References, Type on Hover, Outline and Symbol Search.
The LSP server is 'purely static': it will not re-index source files when they are edited; the indexer must be re-run manually (no restart of VS Code or the server needed).
Using glean-lsp from VS Code requires a generic LSP client such as 'Generic LSP Client (v2)' plus workspace settings naming the Glean DB; only VS Code is documented.

Website landing page: 'Agent- and tool-friendly: Query via CLI, language-specific APIs or Thrift - ideal for IDEs, code review bots, refactoring tools, LLM coding agents'; 'Coding agents, IDEs, and developer tools query Glean instead of relying on grep'.
Query docs (open-source build): 'There is currently only a Haskell API; APIs in other languages are coming soon'; the Thrift API's querying methods are userQuery and userQueryFacts.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry or phone-home found in the open-source build. Logging and stats hooks are compiled-in no-op stubs (glean/github/Logger/IO.hs:13-16; glean/github/Logger/GleanGlass.hs:15-24; glean/github/ServiceData/GlobalStats.hs:16-35); the docs say `--enable-logging` has 'no logging backend implemented for the open-source build' (glean/website/docs/running.md:165-172); outbound auth headers are an identity function (glean/github/Glean/Auth.hs:9-26); Scribe writes throw 'not supported' (glean/github/Glean/Datasource/Scribe/Write.hs:21-22); Glass `--trace-to-vlog` only logs locally (glean/glass/Glean/Glass/Options.hs:92-96). No accounts or API keys are required. Network use: (a) glean-server and glass-server listen on a port (Glass default 26073: glean/glass/Glean/Glass/Config.hs:24-25; glean-server --port: glean/server/Glean/Server/Config.hs:31), speaking Thrift over HTTP by default with a /health endpoint (glean/github/Facebook/Service/HttpFb303.hs:19-34). The HTTP server, TLS and bind-address code live in the external hsthrift repo (not in this tree), so bind address and TLS are unknown. The open-source build has no inbound authentication (auth code is compiled only under GLEAN_FACEBOOK: glean/server/Glean/Server.hs:223-253; glean/glass/Glean/Glass/Main.hs:158-173) while the service RPCs include writes, deletes and restores (glean/if/glean.thrift:1146-1287); the only documented mitigation is `--db-read-only` (glean/website/docs/running.md:154-156). (b) An optional S3 DB backup/restore backend (cabal flag s3-support defaults True: glean.cabal.in:96-98) registers an 's3' backend that uses AWS credential discovery, with usage via s3: locators (glean/db/backup/s3/Glean/Database/Backup/S3.hs:10-22,69-72). (c) glean-lsp runs Glass in-process and reads local DBs or a --service HOST:PORT server (glean/lsp/Glean/LSP.hs:35-43,317-322; glean/lsp/README.md:91-108). (d) Build time: install_deps.sh clones https://github.com/facebookincubator/hsthrift.git unpinned and builds folly/rocksdb (install_deps.sh:18,33-43); cabal needs the Hackage index (index-state pinned at cabal.project:25). Indexers shell out to external tools (flow, hh_server, scip-*, elp) whose own network behaviour is outside this repo.

code.architecture: Index-then-query pipeline. (1) Indexers (glean/lang/*, registry in glean/index/list/Glean/Indexer/List.hs:49-74) mostly wrap external tools - clang-index (glean/lang/clang), hh_server, flow, hie-indexer (glean/lang/haskell), scip-*/lsif tools plus the Rust scip-to-glean converter (glean/lang/scip/indexer/scip_to_glean) - and emit JSON/binary facts typed by Angle schemas (glean/schema/source/*.angle; generated Haskell/Thrift/C++ via the gen-schema target, Makefile:282-292). (2) Facts are stored in immutable, de-duplicated databases by the C++ runtime glean/rts (fact store, bytecode evaluator, ownership, queries) on RocksDB (glean/rocksdb) or experimental LMDB (glean/lmdb, glean/lmdb-clib); Haskell glean/db manages DB lifecycle, schema, Angle typechecking/compilation (glean/db/Glean/Query/*) and backups (glean/db/backup/s3); glean/angle holds the Angle lexer/parser (Lexer.x, Parser.y). (3) glean/server serves GleanService (glean/if/glean.thrift); glean/client/hs plus glean/backend-api and glean/backend-local give local-or-remote Haskell access; the `glean` CLI and shell (glean/tools/gleancli, glean/shell) work on local DBs or a server. (4) Glass (glean/glass) is a language-agnostic symbol service built on the codemarkup.* schemas, exposing GlassService (glean/glass/if/glass.thrift; glean/glass/ARCHITECTURE.md:3-5). (5) glean-lsp (glean/lsp; 3 Haskell modules) embeds Glass in-process (LSP.hs:35-43) and maps documentSymbolIndex, findReferenceRanges and searchSymbol onto LSP (LSP.hs:437,505,571). Build glue: glean.cabal.in (m4-generated glean.cabal), cabal.project, Makefile + mk/*.mk (C++ libs), install_deps.sh (clones hsthrift). Docs/site: glean/website (Docusaurus); glean/vscode (Angle syntax highlighting only). Source layout overview: glean/ROADMAP.md:57-146.

claim_checks.claim: glean-lsp provides Go to Definition, Go to References, Type on Hover, Outline and Symbol Search (glean/lsp/README.md:12-16).
claim_checks.evidence: Handlers are registered in glean/lsp/Glean/LSP.hs:267-291: hover (272), definition (273), references (276), workspace symbol (284), document symbols (288), plus open/close/cancel/config. Definition = cross-reference targets from Glass documentSymbolIndex (LSP.hs:412-420, 587-591); hover returns only the 'symbolSignature' attribute as plain text (LSP.hs:473-487). Commented out / absent: type definition, implementation, rename, prepareRename, didChange, didSave, codeAction, completion (LSP.hs:274-275, 277-278, 281-282, 286-289). It needs --db-root or --service, otherwise 'No default Glean service' (glean/client/hs/local/Glean/LocalOrRemote.hs:136-143).

claim_checks.claim: The LSP server is 'purely static' and does not re-index edited files (glean/lsp/README.md:20-23).
claim_checks.evidence: didChange/didSave handlers are commented out (glean/lsp/Glean/LSP.hs:281-282); the in-file TODO lists 'update index after edits' and 'can we show errors somehow?' as not done (LSP.hs:48-63); the symbol cache is dropped only on config change or didClose (LSP.hs:257-259, 351-357). No publishDiagnostics, WorkspaceEdit, TextEdit or CodeAction exists in glean/lsp or glean/glass (searched; only commented-out handler names), and the Glass API is read-only (glean/glass/if/glass.thrift:953-1040).

claim_checks.claim: glean-lsp 'works for any language supported by Glean and Glass' (glean/lsp/README.md:9-10).
claim_checks.evidence: Support per language depends on Glass/codemarkup and on having an indexed DB; the README itself says 'Some languages might be missing certain features' (glean/lsp/README.md:172-175). Glass maps file extensions to 17 languages (glean/glass/Glean/Glass/Repos.hs:237-296; the Language enum has 29 values: glean/glass/if/glass.thrift:644-674). In the OSS build the Glass repo name is simply the Glean DB name (AutoRepoMapping: glean/glass/Glean/Glass/RepoMapping.hs:32-36; Repos.hs:216-217). risks: Read-only, batch-indexed navigation: glean-lsp serves a static index and ignores didChange/didSave (glean/lsp/Glean/LSP.hs:281-282); re-indexing is manual (glean/lsp/README.md:20-23); post-edit re-index and error display are listed as unimplemented TODOs (LSP.hs:48-63). No diagnostics, rename, code-action or any edit capability exists (LSP.hs:277-278, 286-287; Glass API is read-only: glean/glass/if/glass.thrift:953-1040). glean-lsp has no test-suite (glean/lsp/glean-lsp.cabal) and CI only builds it (.github/workflows/ci.yml:209-210).

Integration gap for agent clients: no MCP server and no Claude Code/Codex plugin, skill or config in the tree. glean-lsp is documented only for VS Code + Generic LSP Client (glean/lsp/README.md:49-76). It requires a workspace root from the client (LSP.hs:227-233), reads the DB name from client config section 'glean-lsp' with default 'stackage' (LSP.hs:88-100, 260), and needs DB file paths relative to the workspace root, the most common failure per the docs (glean/lsp/README.md:141-146; blog 2026-02-06-glean-0-2.md:122-126).

Heavy, Linux-only build: no macOS support (glean/website/docs/building.md:19-20); GHC <= 9.6 (base <4.19, glean.cabal.in:173); about 35 system packages (building.md:45-86); folly and rocksdb are built through the separate hsthrift repo cloned unpinned at HEAD (install_deps.sh:18,33-43); builds are slow because cabal cannot build C++ in parallel (blog 2026-02-06-glean-0-2.md:30-34); 16 GB RAM suggested for faster builds (building.md:231). Useful indexing also needs per-language toolchains (hh_server, flow, scip-*, clang/LLVM libs) plus the Rust scip-to-glean converter (glean/website/docs/indexer/python-scip.md:46-57).

Security posture: the OSS server has no inbound authentication; auth hooks are no-ops (glean/github/Glean/Auth.hs:24-26) and the real auth code compiles only under GLEAN_FACEBOOK (glean/server/Glean/Server.hs:223-253; glean/glass/Glean/Glass/Main.hs:158-173), yet GleanService exposes writes, deletes and restores (glean/if/glean.thrift:1146-1287); the only documented mitigation is --db-read-only (glean/website/docs/running.md:154-156). Bind address/TLS are implemented in the external hsthrift package (unknown here). External indexers run through a shell command string (glean/index/Glean/Indexer/External.hs:139-145). No SECURITY.md (CONTRIBUTING.md:25-27 defers to Meta's bounty program); CodeQL covers only actions/python/javascript-typescript, not Haskell or C/C++ (.github/workflows/codeql.yml:25-29).

Docs and CI drift: the README advertises a Docker demo that the docs call 'currently not working' (README.md:81-90 vs glean/website/docs/docker.md:11-16); Dockerfile:17 references a missing Setup.hs and the image stage uses ubuntu:20.04, ghc-8.10.2 and libssl1.1 (Dockerfile:5,43,58); the README mount path differs from the entrypoint's (README.md:87 vs docker_entrypoint.sh:15). ci-aarch64.yml:115 runs a nonexistent `make glean-hiedb`. glean/website/docs/indexer/cxx.md:22-27,41 says the clang indexer is not on Hackage and was tested with clang 11/12, but building.md:88-92,170-174 and ci.yml:197 use `cabal install glean-clang` and clang-15. The glean-lsp README settings snippet is not valid JSON (glean/lsp/README.md:54-65).

Internal-mirror and maintenance caveats: the source is mirrored from Meta's internal tree. 54 GLEAN_FACEBOOK-conditional lines across 21 files (searched); internal directories such as glean/glass/facebook are referenced by glean/glass/ARCHITECTURE.md:164,266 but absent; logging, auth, Scribe, source-control and repo-mapping are OSS stubs (glean/github/**; glean/glass/Glean/Glass/RepoMapping.hs:32-60), so the documented `glass` CLI is not available. HEAD version 0.2.0.1 (glean.cabal.in:6) is not in CHANGELOG.md:3; the maintainer contact is a Meta alias (glean.cabal.in:14).

Release and supply-chain posture: no release workflow, checksums, signatures, SBOM or attestations in .github; Hackage uploads are manual (blog 2026-02-06-glean-0-2.md:13-16); glean.cabal is generated by m4 and gitignored (Makefile:126-131; .gitignore:7); no Haskell freeze file, only an index-state pin (cabal.project:25); Makefile `install` is a stub (Makefile:371-374); core Haskell dependencies (fb-util, thrift-*, folly-clib) live in the separate hsthrift repo (cabal.project:3-18); the demo image is republished weekly as :latest (.github/workflows/glean-docker.yml:7-10,35-43).

Licensing details: root license is BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE; glean.cabal.in:11), but glean/lsp/LICENSE also embeds MIT (static-ls) and Apache-2.0 (ghcide) notices with a split/garbled tail (glean/lsp/LICENSE:32-70), and glean/lmdb-clib ships the OpenLDAP Public License 2.8 (glean/lmdb-clib/LICENSE:1-3) while its cabal file declares BSD-3-Clause (glean/lmdb-clib/lmdb-clib.cabal:9). Contributions require a Facebook CLA (README.md:59-63).
